title: Keyword search
text: Punctuation keyword searched , interpreted. need escape anything. Set regex = TRUE want pattern. keyword passed PCRE regular expression, whole_word ignored — write anchors .
code: doses <- data.frame(   id = c("D1", "D2", "D3"),   note = c("dose (2 mg) given", "dose 2 mg given", "wrote the c++ parser"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  jtb_search_keyword(doses, "dose (2 mg)") jtb_search_keyword(doses, "c++") jtb_search_keyword(doses, "dose [(]?[0-9]+ mg", regex = TRUE) # Anything ending in a unit of mass. jtb_search_keyword(doses, "\\d+ (mg|kg)\\b", regex = TRUE)$id #> [1] "D1" "D2"

title: Keyword search

title: Semantic search
text: query every row put jtb_tokenize(): lower-cased, split punctuation, stripped stop words, stemmed word endings stop mattering. Compare unstemmed version see stemmer : stemmer runs depends library: SnowballC::wordStem() package installed, small built-suffix stripper otherwise. two always agree, scores can shift slightly machines differ — ranking stable, third decimal place . Install SnowballC every machine needs identical numbers. tokens compared TF-IDF cosine similarity. IDF half makes better counting shared words: term appears nearly every row carries almost weight, rare term carries lot. table “subject” nearly worthless “autoinjector” decisive. comparison, query expanded thesaurus. query word belonging synonym group brings rest group synonym_weight (0.6 default, synonym counts rather less word actually typed). expansion carries “stomach” across “queasy”:
code: jtb_tokenize("Subject reported a severe HEADACHE after dosing.") #> [[1]] #> [1] "subject" "report"  "sever"   "headach" "dose" jtb_tokenize("Subject reported a severe HEADACHE after dosing.", stem = FALSE) #> [[1]] #> [1] "subject"  "reported" "severe"   "headache" "dosing" jtb_synonyms()$nausea #>  [1] "nausea"      "nauseous"    "queasy"      "sick"        "sickness"    "vomit"       #>  [7] "vomited"     "vomiting"    "emesis"      "throwing"    "stomach"     "abdominal"   #> [13] "gut"         "upset"       "unsettled"   "indigestion"

title: Semantic search
text: top_n caps number rows; min_score drops weak ones. apply, top_n = NULL means “cap”. add_score = FALSE leaves input columns untouched want rows without two extra columns.
code: # The default: at most the ten best rows, each scoring at least 0.05. nrow(jtb_search_semantic(site_reports, "tired", columns = "comment")) #> [1] 2  # Everything, scored, in rank order. all_rows <- jtb_search_semantic(site_reports, "tired", columns = "comment",                                 top_n = NULL, min_score = 0) nrow(all_rows) #> [1] 24 head(all_rows$.score, 8) #> [1] 0.301402 0.159492 0.011527 0.011511 0.010826 0.003735 0.003682 0.003365  # Only strong matches, however many that is. jtb_search_semantic(site_reports, "tired", columns = "comment",                     top_n = NULL, min_score = 0.2)[, c("report_id", "comment")]

title: Semantic search
text: built-thesaurus small starter set. know domain, honest failure mode query returns nothing: Neither “skin” “irritation” appears table, neither default synonym group, nothing match . Supply group query works: list merged defaults group name, adding group keeps everything else working, reusing default name replaces group: Pass synonyms = NULL switch expansion entirely. worth real query, see much answer thesaurus responsible : one row literally says “exhausted”; thesaurus brings row says “unusually tired”.
code: nrow(jtb_search_semantic(site_reports, "skin irritation", columns = "comment")) #> [1] 0 skin_terms <- list(   skin = c("skin", "irritation", "irritated", "rash", "hives", "urticaria",            "itchy", "itching", "patch", "redness", "swelling") )  jtb_search_semantic(site_reports, "skin irritation", columns = "comment",                     synonyms = skin_terms, top_n = 4)[                       , c("report_id", "term", "comment", ".score")] # The nausea group is still in force alongside the new skin group. jtb_search_semantic(site_reports, "stomach upset", columns = "comment",                     synonyms = skin_terms, top_n = 2)$report_id #> [1] "R009" "R024" with_thesaurus <- jtb_search_semantic(site_reports, "exhausted and sleepy",                                       columns = "comment", top_n = 3) without <- jtb_search_semantic(site_reports, "exhausted and sleepy",                                columns = "comment", top_n = 3,                                synonyms = NULL)  with_thesaurus[, c("report_id", "comment", ".score")] without[, c("report_id", "comment", ".score")]

title: Semantic search
text: stopwords = character() worth remembering. default list contains "" "", box “rash reported” “rash reported” look alike. Pass empty stop-word list negation matters, negations survive comparison.
code: jtb_search_semantic(   site_reports, "device problem",   columns = c("term", "comment"),   weights = c(token = 0.9, ngram = 0.1),  # trust words more than spelling   synonym_weight = 0.8,                   # synonyms nearly as good as typed words   stopwords = character(),                # keep "no", "not", "off" ...   stem = FALSE                            # exact word forms only )

title: Semantic search
text: genuine model-based semantics, pass embed_fun: function takes character vector returns numeric matrix one row per string. supplied two similarities skipped score becomes cosine similarity query’s embedding row’s, rescaled 0–1. shape contract easiest see toy embedding — one dimension per letter: results nonsense, point: function exactly embedding tells , bad embedding gives bad rankings. real one looks package’s side: Two things keep mind. function called query followed every row, API-backed embedding batch internally cache search table repeatedly. result stops reproducible: now stable model behind .
code: letter_counts <- function(x) {   t(vapply(strsplit(tolower(x), ""), function(ch) {     tabulate(match(ch, letters), nbins = 26L)   }, numeric(26))) }  jtb_search_semantic(site_reports, "headache", columns = "comment",                     embed_fun = letter_counts, top_n = 3)[                       , c("report_id", "comment", ".score")] # Sketch: replace with whichever embedding service or local model you use. embed <- function(x) {   vecs <- lapply(x, function(txt) my_embedding_api(txt))  # numeric vectors   do.call(rbind, vecs) }  jtb_search_semantic("reports.xlsx", "device malfunction",                     columns = "comment", embed_fun = embed, top_n = 20)

title: Find rows containing a keyword — jtb_search_keyword

what: Rank rows by how closely they match a query in meaning — jtb_search_semantic
title: Rank rows by how closely they match a query in meaning — jtb_search_semantic
text: jtb_search_keyword() asks "row contain word?", function asks "close row idea?" returns rows sorted score. search "stomach upset" can surface row reading "subject felt nauseous morning dose" even though two share words.

title: Rank rows by how closely they match a query in meaning — jtb_search_semantic
code: jtb_search_semantic(   data,   query,   columns = NULL,   output_csv = NULL,   top_n = 10L,   min_score = 0.05,   synonyms = jtb_synonyms(),   synonym_weight = 0.6,   weights = c(token = 0.75, ngram = 0.25),   stopwords = jtb_stopwords(),   stem = TRUE,   embed_fun = NULL,   add_score = TRUE,   sheet = 1,   ... )

title: Rank rows by how closely they match a query in meaning — jtb_search_semantic
text: data Excel path, delimited-file path, data frame. See jtb_read_table(). query word, phrase sentence search . columns Columns search, names, 1-based positions, logical mask. NULL, default, searches every column. Text columns useful ones; values selected column pasted together form text row. output_csv Optional path. given, returned rows – including score columns – also written utils::write.csv(). top_n Keep many rows, best first. NULL keeps every row min_score. Defaults 10. min_score Drop rows scoring . Defaults 0.05, removes rows meaningful overlap; use 0 keep everything. synonyms named list character vectors, shape jtb_synonyms(), merged defaults group name. NULL disables synonym expansion entirely. synonym_weight Weight given term pulled synonym group, relative term user actually typed. Defaults 0.6. weights Named numeric vector giving blend two similarities, c(token = 0.75, ngram = 0.25) default. Rescaled sum 1. Ignored embed_fun supplied. stopwords Words ignore, defaulting jtb_stopwords(). stem Stem tokens comparing. TRUE default. embed_fun Optional embedding function; see section . add_score Attach .score .rank columns result. TRUE default; set FALSE get input columns untouched. sheet Worksheet read data path Excel workbook. ... Passed jtb_read_table().

title: Rank rows by how closely they match a query in meaning — jtb_search_semantic
text: data.frame matching rows ordered descending score, original row names preserved , unless add_score = FALSE, two extra columns: .score (0-1) .rank (1 best match). Ties broken original row order. result carries "jtb_search" attribute recording query, expanded query terms, columns searched score settings.

title: Rank rows by how closely they match a query in meaning — jtb_search_semantic
text: default neural network involved – score blend two classical similarities, keeps function dependency-free, offline deterministic: Token similarity (weight weights["token"]). query row tokenised jtb_tokenize() – lower-cased, stripped stop words, stemmed – compared TF-IDF cosine similarity. Rare words therefore count common ones. comparison query expanded synonyms: query word synonym group brings rest group synonym_weight, carries "stomach upset" across "nauseous". Fuzzy similarity (weight weights["ngram"]). cosine, computed character 3-grams instead words. tolerates typos, plurals word endings stemmer misses. two combined weighted average reported .score, 0-1 scale. Scores comparable within one call, across calls across tables – IDF depends corpus searched. genuine embedding-model semantics, pass embed_fun: function taking character vector returning numeric matrix one row per input. supplied, two similarities skipped score cosine similarity query embedding row's, rescaled [-1, 1] [0, 1].

title: jtb2026 0.1.0
text: First release. jtb_search_keyword() returns rows whose selected columns contain keyword. Literal default, regex, whole_word, ignore_case, multiple keywords match = "" | "", add_match_info record column matched. jtb_search_semantic() ranks rows similarity query, blending TF-IDF cosine similarity stemmed, synonym-expanded tokens fuzzy character-3-gram similarity. embed_fun hands scoring embedding model instead. jtb_read_table() reads Excel workbooks, delimited files, matrices data frames; searches take data argument straight . jtb_tokenize(), jtb_stopwords() jtb_synonyms() expose pieces semantic score built . site_reports, 24-row mock table used examples vignettes. searches take output_csv write exactly return.
